Solari, Bevy's realtime pathtraced renderer, has seen major improvements to pretty much every aspect of the plugin!

Read for the technical details, or continue reading below for the high level overview.

JMS55's blog

#

Thanks to improvements in our implementation, rendering is now mostly unbiased, leading to much more accurate lighting.

ReSTIR

Additionally, thanks to some other changes, moving objects no longer have shadows that lag behind, and reflections now look significantly less shimmery in motion, especially for non-metallic materials.

#

DLSS-RR has gotten very good in recent updates, and for many scenes, ReSTIR costs a decent chunk of performance, and does not significantly improve image quality.

As a result, we've decided to make ReSTIR optional, and turn it .off by default

If you were using Solari in Bevy 0.19, check if the loss of ReSTIR affects your scene, and if so re-enable .

SolariLighting::restir

With ReSTIR off, expect reduced shadow quality and missing shadows in motion in scenes with many lights. We are exploring cheaper ways of improving light sampling, without ReSTIR, to improve this in the future.

In addition, Solari's scene management code is now retained (similar to retained render world optimizations in previous versions of Bevy), and overall much more optimized, leading to reduced CPU costs.significantly

You may also want to take a look at the new fields in . While we aim to set reasonable defaults that will work well across a wide variety of games, there are now many knobs (world cache size, per-pixel light sample count, temporal accumulation, and path tracing bounce count) that can be tweaked to improve performance or quality for your specific scene, project and hardware.

SolariLighting

#

Solari now supports lighting from and s on cameras, in addition to the existing support for and emissive meshes. We're hoping to add support for the remaining , , and types .

Atmosphere

EnvironmentMapLight

DirectionalLight

PointLight

SpotLight

RectLight

in the near future

Solari now also runs on macOS, but note that there is currently no built-in denoiser included in for macOS. MetalFX Ray Reconstruction might be a possible solution in the future (contributions welcome!)

bevy_solari

#

Finally, our crate has been updated to support the latest version of DLSS, bringing support for DLSS-RR 4.5, which significantly improves denoising quality in Solari.

dlss_wgpu

If you were using DLSS in Bevy 0.19, make sure to the newest version of the DLSS SDK, else you will run into compiler errors.

BSN landed with a few idiosyncrasies that caused friction in practice. We made some changes to BSN's syntax this cycle in the interest of improving its ergonomics and clarity. After this, the syntax largely be nailed down.should

#

All scene references now require prefixes:

@

// Beforebsn! { scene_variable scene_function() @SceneComponent {scene_expression}}// Afterbsn! { @scene_variable @scene_function() @SceneComponent @{scene_expression}}

In addition to making it easier to spot scene inclusions (and unifying the syntax across cases), this freed us up to make component values easier to work with!much

template_value

#

You can now remove all of those pesky wrappers from your component values:

template_value

// Beforebsn! { template_value(component_variable) template_value(component_function())}// Afterbsn! { component_variable component_function()}

#

Enums no longer require or , provided they implement and :

VariantDefaults

FromTemplate

Default

Clone

// Before#[derive(Component, Default, Clone, VariantDefaults)]enum Foo { A { x: u32, y: u32 }, #[default] B,}bsn! { Foo::B}// After#[derive(Component, Default, Clone)]enum Foo { A { x: u32, y: u32 }, #[default] B,}bsn! { Foo::B}

If you were using an enum that didn't support , you can now remove the wrapper:

VariantDefaults

template_value

// Beforebsn! { template_value(Foo::A)}// Afterbsn! { Foo::A}

The removal of does mean that enums must now have every field specified:

VariantDefaults

// Before (y field is initialized to its default value)bsn! { Foo::A { x: 1 }}// After (y field must be manually specified)bsn! { Foo::A { x: 1, y: 0 }}

We believe this tradeoff is worth it, as it increases BSN's compatibility with arbitrary Rust enums. Rust doesn't support "enum variant defaults" anyway!

#

The "builder pattern" (and chained methods generally) previously required a wrapper. This can now be removed:

template_value

// Beforebsn! { template_value(Transform::from_xyz(-2.5, 4.5, 9.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y))}// Afterbsn! { Transform::from_xyz(-2.5, 4.5, 9.0).looking_at(Vec3::ZERO, Vec3::Y)}

Additionally, you can now remove the wrapper in cases like this:

template_value

// Beforebsn! { template_value(node.clone())}// Afterbsn! { node.clone()}

In general, you should now be able to remove all instances from your BSN declarations!

template_value

#

BSN previously used commas to separate entities, with optional around entities to make the boundaries clearer. This resulted in a lot of syntax noise, line noise, and over-indentation:

()

bsn! { Node Children [ ( #OkButton @button("Ok") ), ( #CancelButton @button("Cancel") ), ]}

To avoid this, many developers opted for this syntax instead, which made it very hard to visually distinguish entities:

bsn! { Node Children [ #OkButton @button("Ok"), #CancelButton @button("Cancel"), ]}

BSN now uses to separate entities in a list:

--

bsn! { Node Children [ #OkButton @button("Ok") -- #CancelButton @button("Cancel") ]}

This gives us the best of all worlds: entities are visually distinct, and there is no over-indentation, line noise, or syntax noise ( when compared to other competitors in the "markup format" space are very competitive!). Both and have been deprecated in this context.

We landed BSN, Bevy's next generation scene system, . It was missing a key piece though: the ability to easily run logic when a scene is fully "ready" and spawned (ex: all dependencies have loaded, the full hierarchy is present, and all of the initial components are inserted in the scene). This is a critical piece for building cohesive, standalone, composable scenes. It is also necessary to properly layer Bevy logic on top of scene representations (like glTF).

in our last release

other

The closest we had was the event for a given component, which runs "top down" (meaning children are not available). We needed a "bottom up" equivalent to enable building logic that relies on the complete loaded and spawned scene.

Add

The solution is pretty straightforward: trigger a new event for each entity in a spawned scene the full spawn logic has run for that entity (including its descendants).

Ready

after

This enables the following:

#[derive(SceneComponent, Default, Clone)]struct Widget;impl Widget { fn scene() -> impl Scene { bsn! { Node { width: px(100), height: px(100) } on(|ready: On| { info!("The full scene, including 'widget.bsn' contents, is available here") }) Children [ Text("hello") -- :"widget.bsn" ] } }}world.spawn(bsn! { @Widget })

Bevy's shaders are now written in and the old "Custom Bevy Extended WGSL" language support has been removed.

WESL

WESL is a language standard that extends WGSL to add important usability features like modules, imports, conditional compilation, and more. You can see what that looks like (and render pretty shader toys!) live in your browser in the .

WESL Playground

Bevy has historically handled these things in our own custom WGSL dialect, but we believe it is better for the wider shader ecosystem (and for us) to adopt a common standard where we can pool resources on language improvements, module ecosystems, and IDE tooling. We've been working closely with the WESL team to evolve the standard in a way that fits well into the Bevy picture.

A critical part of that tooling is language server protocol support, in the form of . That means syntax highlighting, go-to-definition, inlay hints, code folding, formatting and more, once installed for your IDE of choice.

wgsl-analyzer

Custom shaders in the old Bevy WGSL dialect need to be translated to WESL and renamed from to . Plain WGSL files with no preprocessor directives will keep working.

Mesh shaders are now integrated with Bevy's pipeline cache and are available for advanced users to take advantage of. Mesh shaders can be used to render:

meshoptimizer

as seen here

nvidium

and more

Mesh shaders, at a high level, replace the classic vertex shader with a compute shader. This allows generating geometry directly on the GPU and passing those generated primitives directly to the fragment shader without using multiple pipelines or intermediary buffers (to pass data from a compute shader to a render pipeline).

A contains:

MeshPipeline

a fragment shader

The new can be used to define a . That is then used as a , which allows the re-use of Bevy's lower level rendering APIs such as to take advantage of the new APIs.

let mut pass = render_context.begin_tracked_render_pass(RenderPassDescriptor { label: Some("custom_mesh_shader_pass"), color_attachments: &[Some(target.get_color_attachment())], depth_stencil_attachment: Some(depth.get_attachment(StoreOp::Store)), ..default()});pass.set_render_pipeline(mesh_pipeline);pass.set_bind_group(0, &bind_group, &[view_uniform_offset.offset]);// draw_mesh_tasks dispatches the task shader if there is one,// or dispatches the mesh shader if there is no task shader.pass.draw_mesh_tasks(1, 1, 1);

It is notable that mesh shaders are an advanced graphics approach with platform-specific performance considerations, and that this is the initial base support for the feature. Higher level user APIs, and easy integration with Bevy's , are left to future work.

Like their regular counterparts, they request an ordering between successive elements, however that ordering is only kept between systems whose data accesses actually conflict. When two weakly-ordered systems actually conflict on their data access, a normal ordering is kept between them, so the earlier one still runs first. Two systems that conflict only through a non-conflicting system between them in the chain stay ordered as well. Non-conflicting systems, however, are left free to run in any order and overlap for increased parallelism!

Two kinds of system are treated as always conflicting, so their ordering is always kept: an earlier system that produces deferred effects such as (so the later system observes them, with an sync point inserted as usual), and exclusive systems (which cannot overlap anything regardless).

Components can now opt-in to "column summary change ticks":

#[derive(Component)]#[component(summary_tick)]struct MyComponent { /* fields here */}

When enabled, this will store a "column change tick" in addition to a "per-entity change tick", which allows cheaply skipping the whole column of entities when querying for changes, rather than needing to check every entity's component to see if it has changed.

This makes mutations more expensive, as they need to write both the column change tick and the entity change tick, but for entities whose changes are queried often, but change infrequently, this tradeoff can easily be worth it! 一句话：开源 Rust 引擎把实时路径追踪插件 Solari 与 DLSS 接进了主线。

要点：

  • 实时路径追踪渲染器 Solari 在几乎每个方面都做了大幅改进，并接入 DLSS
  • BSN 场景语法改进、WESL 着色器、Sprite 材质与扩展的 2D 材质
  • 更多 UI 控件与 Ready 事件，并附 0.19→0.20 迁移指南

为什么值得看：路径追踪 + 上采样这套管线已经进入开源引擎主线，Rust 引擎在渲染与着色器工具链上的追赶速度值得关注。

中文摘要：Bevy 0.20 是 Rust 数据驱动游戏引擎的中期版本，重点集中在渲染。实时路径追踪渲染器 Solari 几乎在每个方面都有明显改进，并接入了 DLSS 上采样，使路径追踪在开源引擎里第一次有了可用的性能组合。场景描述方面改进了 BSN 语法，着色器侧引入 WESL，Sprite 材质与扩展的 2D 材质补齐了 2D 工作流。此外还有更多 UI 控件与 Ready 事件等易用性改动，官方同时提供了 0.19 到 0.20 的迁移指南。对关注引擎架构的人来说，值得看的是它把路径追踪、上采样与场景语法这几块如何拆成互相独立的插件边界。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：Bevy（English）

Bevy 0.20

Posted on October 8, 2026 by Bevy Contributors

The Zorah scene rendered in Bevy Solari

Thanks to contributors, pull requests, community reviewers, and our , we're happy to announce the release on !227817

generous donors

crates.io

For those who don't know, Bevy is a refreshingly simple data-driven game engine built in Rust. You can check out our to try it today. It's free and open source forever! You can grab the full on GitHub. Check out for a collection of community-developed plugins, games, and learning resources.

Solari, Bevy's realtime pathtraced renderer, has seen major improvements to pretty much every aspect of the plugin!

Read for the technical details, or continue reading below for the high level overview.

JMS55's blog

#

Thanks to improvements in our implementation, rendering is now mostly unbiased, leading to much more accurate lighting.

ReSTIR

Additionally, thanks to some other changes, moving objects no longer have shadows that lag behind, and reflections now look significantly less shimmery in motion, especially for non-metallic materials.

#

DLSS-RR has gotten very good in recent updates, and for many scenes, ReSTIR costs a decent chunk of performance, and does not significantly improve image quality.

As a result, we've decided to make ReSTIR optional, and turn it .off by default

If you were using Solari in Bevy 0.19, check if the loss of ReSTIR affects your scene, and if so re-enable .

SolariLighting::restir

With ReSTIR off, expect reduced shadow quality and missing shadows in motion in scenes with many lights. We are exploring cheaper ways of improving light sampling, without ReSTIR, to improve this in the future.

In addition, Solari's scene management code is now retained (similar to retained render world optimizations in previous versions of Bevy), and overall much more optimized, leading to reduced CPU costs.significantly

You may also want to take a look at the new fields in . While we aim to set reasonable defaults that will work well across a wide variety of games, there are now many knobs (world cache size, per-pixel light sample count, temporal accumulation, and path tracing bounce count) that can be tweaked to improve performance or quality for your specific scene, project and hardware.

SolariLighting

#

Solari now supports lighting from and s on cameras, in addition to the existing support for and emissive meshes. We're hoping to add support for the remaining , , and types .

RectLight

in the near future

Solari now also runs on macOS, but note that there is currently no built-in denoiser included in for macOS. MetalFX Ray Reconstruction might be a possible solution in the future (contributions welcome!)

bevy_solari

#

Finally, our crate has been updated to support the latest version of DLSS, bringing support for DLSS-RR 4.5, which significantly improves denoising quality in Solari.

dlss_wgpu

If you were using DLSS in Bevy 0.19, make sure to the newest version of the DLSS SDK, else you will run into compiler errors.

BSN previously used commas to separate entities, with optional around entities to make the boundaries clearer. This resulted in a lot of syntax noise, line noise, and over-indentation:

We landed BSN, Bevy's next generation scene system, . It was missing a key piece though: the ability to easily run logic when a scene is fully "ready" and spawned (ex: all dependencies have loaded, the full hierarchy is present, and all of the initial components are inserted in the scene). This is a critical piece for building cohesive, standalone, composable scenes. It is also necessary to properly layer Bevy logic on top of scene representations (like glTF).

in our last release

other

The closest we had was the event for a given component, which runs "top down" (meaning children are not available). We needed a "bottom up" equivalent to enable building logic that relies on the complete loaded and spawned scene.

WESL

WESL is a language standard that extends WGSL to add important usability features like modules, imports, conditional compilation, and more. You can see what that looks like (and render pretty shader toys!) live in your browser in the .

WESL Playground

Bevy has historically handled these things in our own custom WGSL dialect, but we believe it is better for the wider shader ecosystem (and for us) to adopt a common standard where we can pool resources on language improvements, module ecosystems, and IDE tooling. We've been working closely with the WESL team to evolve the standard in a way that fits well into the Bevy picture.

A critical part of that tooling is language server protocol support, in the form of . That means syntax highlighting, go-to-definition, inlay hints, code folding, formatting and more, once installed for your IDE of choice.

wgsl-analyzer

Custom shaders in the old Bevy WGSL dialect need to be translated to WESL and renamed from to . Plain WGSL files with no preprocessor directives will keep working.

A UI node entity with the component is positioned relative to the target camera's viewport rather than its parent element. s don't inherit their parent's layout, clipping or transform context. They behave like a "root node".

FixedNode

FixedNode

#

Authors:

@ickshonpe

PRs:

#24779

Bevy UI can now draw nodes with elliptical border geometry.

The fields of are now s to enable different radius to be set for each axis.

BorderRadius

CornerRadius

let a = BorderRadius::all(CornerRadius::circular(vh(10.)));let b = BorderRadius::all(vh(10.)); // a == blet c = BorderRadius::top_right(CornerRadius::new(px(10.), px(20.)));

#

Authors:

@andriyDev

PRs:

#25094

Before a schedule runs (and therefore, your systems), it first computes the system run order based on their ordering constraints (, , ) and system sets. However, in addition to this, the schedule must also resolve - if system A and system B both mutate component C, and there's no ordering between A and B, the schedule needs to pick one to run first. So far, the rule has been that this is non-deterministic.

一句话：特性冻结后的整体盘点：原生拖尾、模糊搜索，以及一份要提前看的破坏性变更清单。

要点：

  • 4.8 已进入特性冻结，开发资源全部转向回归修复，因此相对 dev 7 没有新特性，本文是整体盘点
  • 新增原生 Trail3D：做拖尾类特效不再需要自己处理网格绘制与 UV 分配
  • 核心侧引入 FuzzySearch 模糊搜索、3D 视口按轴覆盖等编辑器改进，并逐项列出破坏性变更（ScriptServer、ClassDB、PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE、SCREEN_UV 等）

为什么值得看：升级前先对一遍破坏性变更清单，尤其是脚本服务器与属性存储相关项，比读功能列表更重要。

中文摘要：Godot 4.8 进入 beta 1，意味着特性已完全冻结，开发者资源转向回归修复与缺陷排查，因此这一篇不再是新特性清单，而是对整个 4.8 的盘点与补充说明。渲染与 3D 侧最实用的新增是原生 Trail3D：想做拖尾特效不必再深入网格绘制、UV 分配这些细节。编辑器与核心侧有「允许视口覆盖」的 3D 视口轴向切换、以及面向版本控制的更整洁的对象序列化，此外 FuzzySearch 模糊搜索正式对所有用户开放。文章也逐项列出破坏性变更，涉及 ScriptServer、ClassDB、PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE、OS.alert()、SCREEN_UV 等，并给出对应的 PR 编号，方便升级前逐条核对。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：Godot（English）

RitaA game by SporkTank

Dev snapshot: Godot 4.8 beta 1

By:

Thaddeus Crews15 October 2026

Pre-release

It’s that time of the release cycle once again: the beta snapshot! With this, 4.8 is fully in feature-freeze, and developer resources have shifted exclusively to creating and reviewing various .

regression fixes

For those interested in aiding us on our quest to squash any bugs that come up during this time, we once again encourage you to join our bug-hunting sprints. Anyone interested should read the for more information, and join the and channels on our developer RocketChat to participate.

Bug Triage Introduction

#bugsquad

#bugsquad-sprints

Please consider , if you are able. Godot is maintained by the efforts of volunteers and a small team of paid contributors. Your donations go towards sponsoring their work and ensuring they can dedicate their undivided attention to the needs of the project.

supporting the project financially

, and give it a spin right now, or continue reading to learn more about improvements in this release. You can also try the , the , or the for this release. If you are interested in the latter, please request to join to get access to pre-release builds.

Downloads

Web editor

XR editor

Android editor

our testing group

a puzzle game with platforming elements, featuring a wide variety of word puzzles within a cozy world. You can buy the game on , and follow the developer on , , and .

Steam

Bluesky

YouTube

itch.io

Highlights

For those who have been following our development snapshots closely, you may be familiar with a number of the highlights in this post which were already covered in previous articles (, , , , , , and ).

4.8 dev 1

4.8 dev 2

Because we’re already in feature freeze, there are no new features to cover compared to dev 7. Instead, we’ll focus on a general round-up of what to expect from Godot 4.8 as a whole, as well as expanding on some additions that we didn’t have the chance to highlight in our previous snapshots.

Breaking changes

Breaking changes

You can find a list of such issues by filtering the merged PRs in the 4.8 milestone with the .

starts our feature round-up strong with . Trail3D

GH-117107

Cozy Cube Godot Addons

While being more of an editor feature, the 3D Viewport override functionality by in warrants a highlight in this section. Michael Alexsander

brought us “Fuzzy searching” with , enabling search results to return matches to the passed query, rather than only returning an exact match. Now with , this functionality is finally ready to roll for all users.

Adam Johnston

Those using version control will be thrilled to hear that serialization of objects has become cleaner starting with . ensures that all objects are now formatted such that they won’t cause oversized diffs.much

Documentation

’s efforts in grants our documentation—both in-editor and online—native support for admonitions; That being: the built-in systems many documentation tools provide to highlight crucial information. As time of writing, our documentation tools use simple prefixes like “” or “” to convey a similar effect, but this method causes critical details to blend in with the rest of the text. So starting now, we’ll begin slowly rolling out admonition replacements for these legacy systems, which will end up looking something like what you see below:

Cyril Bissey

GH-111375

Note:Warning:

Dark ModeLight Mode

Editor

Ever since the introduction of the in Godot 4.6, has been on a journey to migrate our existing editor plugins to this new system. The most ambitious migration yet occurred with , which converts the into a dock. This is a very fundamental change to how the editor is handled, but the benefits that are immediately available are more than worth it.

EditorDock

Tomasz Chabora

GH-113051

main screen itself

As a result of these changes:

EditorDock

Main screen docks have their own editor setting for tab style.

All main screens can be closed.

WindowWrapper

Complimenting the new structure of our editor are new and improved toolbars for our various main screens. delivered three fantastic overhauls to the Game, 2D, and 3D panels with , , and respectively. All three being spearheaded by the same creative vision ensures a uniform style; one which heavily emphasizes usability and clarity in comparison to the prior implementations.

Jayden Sipe

GH-118664

GH-121080

GH-121065

BeforeAfterGame2D3D

delivers the ability to drag-toggle visibility in the scene tree editor with . Now when toggling the visibility of a given node, the newly toggled state can be applied to any subsequent nodes when dragging the mouse across them.

Mikael Hermansson

GH-118634

It’s never been easier to make a title more accessible to users across multiple languages, thanks to the use of . , seeking to further expand the utility and awareness of our , enabled pseudolocalization within the editor itself in . This simple toggle simulates changes that might take place during localization, allowing any issues that would come from that process to be recognized as early as possible in development.

pseudolocalization

Tomasz Chabora

language hot-swap functionality

GH-119443

’s work in brought a long-desired QOL addition to the inspector: auto-expansion of resources. While most of our inspector items automatically revealed themselves when initialized, resources always existed as an unfortunate blindspot. As demonstrated below, this will no longer be the case!

Hugo Locurcio

GH-99725

made it possible to play a scene from the file system directly in . Now any scene can be played from the file system’s context menu alone; no extra steps required!

DexterFstone

GH-111941

Jayden returns with two more editor goodies in , aiming to expand the QOL for our logic. The first of these features is the ability to zoom in/out of the window with a mouse’s scrollwheel. By simply holding while hovering over a window, the contents will either grow or shrink upon scrolling the mouse up or down respectively.

GH-119103

FileSystem

Ctrl

FileSystem

Next up is glob-based searching. Sometimes you want to find a type of file or something with a specific prefix, without necessarily narrowing it down to a specific file. By utilizing glob-based search, now your results can explicitly capture whatever use-case you desire.

keeps the editor train rolling with another highly-requested feature: runtime manipulation of s! Thanks to his work in , the following functionality is now fully integrated within Godot 4.8 (lifted verbatim from the original PR):

Michael Alexsander

CanvasItem

GH-122510

CanvasItem

Full undo/redo support, unified in the editor’s undo/redo manager.

Added the ability to open scenes by double-clicking them in the game. Just like how it’s done in the editor.

Improved remote shortcut handling. Which is now funneled into a single debugger message, and triggers the pressed visual on the buttons.

Improved mouse cursor updates in the editor. Now they trigger immediately rather than after an action is taken with the mouse again.

We’ll end our editor highlights with symbol renaming, an experimental feature brought to us by Tomasz with . With this, renaming a symbol will properly propogate that logic across the project, uniformly applying the rename where relevant.

GH-117949

And more:

GH-119466

GH-120093

GH-122659

GH-117216

GH-88647

Inspector

GH-117499

GH-120736

GH-108878

GH-122809

GH-122903

GH-121278

GH-102734

GH-121364

Tree

GH-121534

GH-110615

GDScript

Courtesy of in , the debugging process for GDScript will become much more streamlined thanks to the direct and immediate information provided by underlined warnings. While you would previously have a line with a warning/error be highlighted if a problem existed, it highlighted the , which both obfuscated the problem and risked multiple issues being hidden if they existed on the same line. With these changes, only the relevant portions of a given line will be underlined. For instance, the following codeblock would’ve previously been highlighted in its entirety:

Malcolm Anderson

entire line

And more:

GH-121833

ScriptInstance

GH-121762

GH-123320

GUI

Every developer knows the struggle of text container constraints all too well. No matter how reasonable you think your font scale is, or what kind of variable text you believe make it in, a translation string or player input inevitably break those bounds. Even if you actively and thoroughly filter all input length at all times, that’s still a lot of code upkeep and boilerplating across different areas of your project to achieve the desired effect.canwill

is one of many who felt this struggle of our text container constraints, and decided to do something about it. grants and resize-to-fit functionality, utilizing three newly-added properties: , , and .

Ismail Ivanov

GH-116791

Label

RichTextLabel

auto_font_size

min_font_size

max_font_size

One of the most common requests we’ve seen for improving functionality is the ability to support “sticky items”. That is: the ability for a given line to stick to the top if it represents a foldable region. is no stranger to , so it was only a matter of time before they delivered the desired functionality in .

Tree

Koliur Rahman

integrating popular editor requests

GH-115697

And more:

format

prefix

suffix

GH-103998

Control

GH-120631

GH-111455

GH-113385

ProgressDialog

GH-121505

Input

Many of our existing GUI items have received native touch support in 4.8, warranting a separate input-focused section dedicated to showcasing their new functionality. All of the following featured items come courtesy of .

Anish Kumar

Starting with ’s two-for-one package deal, both and received the following new functionality:

GH-119706

TextEdit

CodeEdit

Tap (press → release):

Drag (press → drag → release):

This extends to the code completion popup, which previously could not be scrolled via touch input.

Text selection:

Double-tap selects a word.

Double-tap, hold, and drag selects the portion you’re hovering over.

received similar treatment, and is especially easy to showcase thanks to the main screen’s recent conversion to docks, though this functionality will be available to any and all instances.

TabBar

TabBar

is similarly simple to convey through the editor, and is equally available to any and all instances of .

PopupMenu

PopupMenu

Physics

, in collaboration with and , implemented non-allocating classes for and in . By leveraging these new methods, result objects can be successfully reused to avoid unnecessary dictionary and array allocations on every call.

aterray

Ricardo Buring

Mikael Hermansson

PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D

PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D

GH-113970

varresult:=PhysicsCastMotionResult3D.new()func_physics_process(delta:float)->void:ifdirect_space_state.cast_motion_into(params,result):...

These new objects are strongly typed, meaning the need for manual type declarations and dictionary lookups are no longer required.

# Old implementation:vardict:=direct_space_state.intersect_ray(params)ifdict:# Cannot infer the type of "normal"# var normal := dict["normal"]varnormal:Vector3=dict["normal"]# New implementation:varresult:=PhysicsIntersectRayResult3D.new()ifdirect_space_state.intersect_ray_into(params,result):varnormal:=result.get_normal()# Inferred as Vector3.varposition:=result.get_position()# Inferred as Vector3.

And more:

get_velocity_at_(local)_position()
